scripts.radio:
Good evening and welcome to Kenya on Record.

Tonight, we turn our attention to Kibwezi, Makueni County, where the community of Thange Valley has carried an unfair burden for over a decade. Back in 2015, a major leak from a Kenya Pipeline Company line poisoned local water sources, seeped into farmlands, and compromised the health and livelihoods of hundreds of families.

For years, KPC mounted endless legal challenges, dragging devastated residents through the courts while medical expenses piled up and productive soils went barren. Now, finally, the corporation has withdrawn its appeals against the court award granting three billion shillings in compensation.

This withdrawal is welcome, but dropping the appeal is only half the assignment. The real measure of justice is prompt, transparent disbursement. Three billion shillings cannot erase a lost decade of pain, but it is the rightful due of these citizens. There must be no procedural delays, no political games, and no room for brokers to siphon funds intended for sick and displaced families. The National Treasury and KPC management must release every single cent directly to the verified victims without further excuses.

Kwa ufupi: Baada ya miaka mingi ya kesi mahakamani, KPC hatimaye imetupilia mbali rufaa zake dhidi ya fidia ya shilingi bilioni tatu kwa wakaazi wa Thange, Makueni, walioathiriwa na mkasa wa mafuta mwaka wa 2015. Sasa, serikali lazima ilipe fidia hii haraka na kwa uwazi bila ucheleweshaji wowote.
scripts.voice_note: Hello everyone, this is Kenya on Record. Here is what you need to know this week. In Makueni, the families of Thange who endured the toxic 2015 oil spill have reached a significant milestone. Kenya Pipeline Company has finally dropped its court appeals against the three-billion-shilling compensation award. For ten long years, these residents battled poisoned boreholes, ruined farms, and severe medical conditions while the state fought them in court. Now that the appeals are dropped, there are no more excuses left. KPC and the Ministry of Energy must ensure this money is paid directly and transparently to the verified victims—no delays, and no middlemen eating into their settlement. Justice has been delayed far too long; it must be delivered now. Share this with your networks.
scripts.sms: Usiibiwe: During public compensation payouts, never pay brokers claiming to speed up your cash. Deal only with verified legal and community representatives.
scripts.reels: Ten years after toxic oil contaminated their water and farms in Makueni, justice is finally within reach for Thange residents. Kenya Pipeline Company has officially dropped its court appeals against the Sh3 billion compensation award. But dropping the case is only step one. The money must reach the affected families immediately—cleanly, transparently, and without greedy middlemen taking a cut. Pay the victims now.
